en: Oṃ, homage to the Omniscient One!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great saṅgha of twelve thousand five hundred bhikṣus,
such as the venerable Ājñātakauṇḍinya, the venerable Mahānāman, the venerable Revata, and the venerable...
Together with the venerable Vakkula, the venerable Śāriputra, the venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra, and millions of other disciples,

they all approached the place where the Blessed One was, at the Jetavana monastery. Having bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they stood before him, along with thirty-two thousand bodhisattvas,
such as the bodhisattva mahāsattva Sahacittotpādadharmacakrapravartana and Anikṣiptadhura.
And with the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta,
and thirty-two thousand Bodhisattvas headed by these;
They all approached the place where the Blessed One was, at the Jetavana monastery;

having bowed their heads at the feet of the Blessed One, they stood before him. Then, in the morning, the Blessed One dressed himself and, taking only his bowl and robe, entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:
"Go, Ānanda, and bring a bowl, a water-strainer, and a sling."
Then, as soon as he heard the Blessed One, the venerable Ānanda brought his bowl, water-strainer, and shoulder-bag to the Blessed One.
Then the venerable Ānanda, with palms joined in reverence, addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"When you enter for alms..."
"May you indeed liberate many living beings"—[or] "I would liberate... I would deliver;
may you deliver many sentient beings."
From the fear of hell, and from the great fear of birth and old age.
O Leaders of the World, may I liberate you from the great fear of the mire of the sufferings of saṃsāra;
you who possess great majesty and are worthy of the supreme gift.
Having liberated many beings from the mire of the suffering of saṃsāra and its great terrors,
he has indeed returned once again.
Then the venerable Ānanda, having spoken these verses to the Blessed One, stood silent.
Then the Blessed One stood not far from the great city of Śrāvastī.
Thereupon, all the windows, gate-towers, and porticoes appeared made of gold, crystal, and silver.
Likewise, in the great city of Śrāvastī, a vast multitude of people had gathered.
Then that multitude became filled with doubt, wondering: "What is the cause, what is the reason that this auspicious omen has appeared for the city?
Lest this city be reduced to ashes!"
Then, among that multitude of people, there stood a man who was aged, decrepit, and advanced in years, having lived for many hundreds of thousands of years.
Then that man, comforting that multitude, spoke thus:
"Do not fear, O sons of good family!
In this very spot on earth is the monastery named Jetavana.

There dwells the Tathāgata named Śākyamuni, an Arhat, a perfectly awakened Buddha, endowed with knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, and a teacher of gods and humans."
And the Buddha, the Blessed One,
entered the great city of Śrāvastī for alms.
At the time of his arrival, this auspicious omen occurred:
Then that multitude of people, with palms joined in reverence, said this to the old man:
"When the qualities and praises of that Blessed One, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, were being proclaimed, this auspicious omen appeared.
What kind of accumulation of merit will there be for one who has merely seen that Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One?"
Then that old man addressed that multitude of people with verses by proclaiming the praise of the Blessed One’s virtues:
"Indeed, that person who hears the name of the Lord of the World is liberated from the sufferings of saṃsāra."
He who hears the name of the Lord of the World shall never go to the states of woe, but shall thus swiftly go to heaven.
Firm in his vow for many millions of eons,
the Sugata of great majesty [remained] through inconceivable millions of billions of eons of the Great-Souled One.
That Bodhisattva, though remaining for as many eons as there are grains of sand in the Ganges,
never at any time goes to the fear of the miserable destinies.
Indeed, whoever hears the name of the Lord of the World shall never again be one who goes to the states of woe.
For inconceivable millions of billions of eons,
he shall always be a universal monarch,
whoever holds the name of the Lord of the World.
Whatever evil was previously done,
all of it will quickly go to destruction;
even Śakra, the lord of gods of great majesty, [will be affected].
For inconceivable millions of billions of eons.
That bodhisattva, bound in the cross-legged posture, goes to the buddha-field of Sukhāvatī;
he possesses the voice of Brahmā, a beautiful sound, and a gentle resonance.
They endure for many thousands of millions of years.
"He who holds the name of the Lord of the World shall never go to the states of woe.
Then that old man, having proclaimed the praise of the Blessed One's virtues to the multitude of people, stood silent.
Then the Blessed One entered the great city of Śrāvastī through the eastern city gate.
And there, at that city gate, twelve koṭis of lotuses appeared;
upon those lotuses, twelve koṭis of bodhisattvas were seated cross-legged.
They appeared with palms joined in reverence.

Then, as soon as the Blessed One had entered the great city of Śrāvastī, ninety-nine hundred thousand million billion beings were established in the world-system Sukhāvatī, as were eighty-four hundred thousand million billion beings.
These were established as the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the world-system Abhirati. Then the Blessed One arrived at the house of the maiden Nagara-valambikā together with Ānanda.
Thereupon, the Blessed One caused the water-wheel in the house of the maiden Nagara-valambikā to creak.
Then, having heard that sound of the wheel, the girl was seized with doubt, wondering:
"What is the cause? What is the reason?
Never before has a mendicant for alms ever come to my house."
Then that girl, the city outcaste, sat in an empty house, her throat choked with tears, weeping and lamenting; she remained there wailing and crying as she searched for a sharp-edged sword.
Then, sitting in the empty house, lamenting, her throat choked with tears, and weeping, the girl addressed these verses:
Alas! What suffering there is in a poor household; death would be better for me than life.
Of what use is this life to me?
If indeed my body is now afflicted by suffering,
who here shall become my protector and refuge?
For I have become destitute this very day, having been born into a poor household.
(Asv 108) Then that girl, the dependent of the city, having sat in an empty house and recited these verses, remained silent.
Then a son of the gods belonging to the Śuddhāvāsa realm, standing in the air, reflected:
If the Blessed One were to see this:
that Tathāgata Śākyamuni, who has practiced hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of manifold difficult deeds, was staying in the house of a girl who lived as a dependent in the city.
Then a son of the gods from the Śuddhāvāsa realm, taking a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [pieces of gold] and a basket of food of a hundred flavors, [approached].
Taking the Kāśika garments and taking [the ornaments], he went to the house of the girl Nagarāvalambikā. Then the son of the gods from the Śuddhavāsa realm said this to the girl Nagarāvalambikā:
"Put on these Kāśika garments, girl, and these ornaments worth many hundreds of thousands."
Having put on these [clothes] and taking this pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [pieces of gold], and having taken this basket of food of a hundred flavors, offer it to the Blessed One.

Then that girl, having put on those Kāśika garments and having taken the pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [pieces of gold], and having taken that basket of food of a hundred flavors, approached the place where the Blessed One was; having approached, she—
She presented her to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One said to that female attendant of the city:
"Dārikā, dedicate this as it was dedicated by the noble Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, such as Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, and the rest."
"There will be an end to womanhood; there will be an end to the life of a poor household.
Then that girl, having dedicated that alms-food, offered it to the Blessed One.
"By this root of merit from the alms-food, may I not be reborn in any poor household.
Then that girl, the city-dweller, having dedicated that alms-food and given it to the Blessed One, began to return to her own home.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to that girl, the city-dweller:
"Return, young lady!
I remember the cause of my former birth;
therefore, I shall relate it."
Then that girl, having turned back, prostrated herself before the Blessed One, falling down with all her limbs.
Then that girl, the city outcaste, addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"Surely this must be due to karma previously committed by me."
Since I was born into a poor household,
have compassion for me who am suffering; turn back the guardians of hell!
O Leader, show compassion for me who am suffering; you have been born in the state of a woman, O Lord of the World, [to save us from] old age, disease, and grief.
Deliver me, who am suffering!
Be my protection, my refuge, and my ultimate resort; deliver me, who am suffering!
For you, O Protector, have indeed made this vow.
Whatever beings there are here in Jambudvīpa.
I shall indeed cause all sentient beings who dwell throughout the ten directions to be happy.
And I shall deliver them all from the ocean of suffering; be our protection, our refuge, and our ultimate resort.
For surely, O Protector, you shall liberate the world from me;
this must be due to my own previously committed karma,
by which I have always been born in a poor household.
Be a protector for me, who am suffering!
But you, O Protector, are the deliverer from old age and disease; be my refuge, O supreme one who has accumulated virtues!
I shall never again commit evil.
"These are the feelings that I experience."
Be born with compassion... O Great Being, become our protection, our refuge, and our ultimate resort— whatever beings there may be here in Jambudvīpa.
And indeed, hold fast to this name in the future time.
After he has entered final nirvāṇa, in a future time,
there will be the destruction of the teaching;
whatever evil has been done, even if it was unprecedented.
All this will quickly come to an end.
Then that daughter, the female street-sweeper, having spoken these verses to the Blessed One, set out once more toward her home.
Then the Blessed One addressed that daughter, the female street-sweeper, with a voice like the song of the kalaviṅka bird, saying:
"Return, daughter; I remember the cause of my former birth, and I shall proclaim it.
Then that girl, having returned, spoke thus:
"Proclaim it today, O Leader of the World!"
Whatever extremely terrible sin has been committed by me at all times—
certainly a most dreadful sin was committed by me, because of which I have always lived in a poor household.
O caravan leader, release me here in this world from this female state;
be my protection, my refuge, and my final resort.
I am always grateful toward my leader.
I shall proclaim this guide to the Dharma;
he shall never abandon the lower realms,
for he purifies the karma as it was performed by me.
Be our protection, our refuge, and our ultimate resort.
O possessor of unattached wisdom, supreme leader of the world, I pay homage to you, O Protector; with palms joined, I take refuge in you.
Then the Blessed One spoke thus to that girl:

"In the past, girl, in a time long gone, incalculable eons ago, there was a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ratnaśikhin, perfect in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed."
The Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One. At that time, there was a royal capital named Padmāvatī.
Furthermore, at that time, in the royal capital of Padmāvatī, there was a householder named Padmaprabha.
You were the daughter of that householder Padmaprabha.
Furthermore, at that time, a monk who lived on alms was entering the villages, towns, market towns, and districts to collect alms.
When he arrived at your house, you, young girl, having taken the alms-food, went out from the house and then entered it once again.
"And I will not give alms-food to that wretched one with a shaven head.
Because of the accumulation of that karma, O girl, you have repeatedly experienced sufferings in the homes of the poor for twelve thousand kalpas.
By that single [act] of yours..."
"Daughter, by this root of merit you shall receive the prophecy of enlightenment.

Since you have not seen the form, marks, or physical stature of that monk, you, daughter, in a future time after inconceivable and immeasurable eons, shall become a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, perfect in knowledge and conduct, named Nagara-dhvaja."
The Sugata, the Knower of the World, the Unsurpassed Charioteer of men to be tamed, the Teacher of gods and humans, the Buddha, the Blessed One, appeared in the world.
Then that girl circumambulated the Blessed One three times and spoke thus:
"Blessed One, what will my buddha-field be like where I shall become a Buddha?"
The Blessed One said:
"That buddha-field shall be named Accumulation of Immeasurable Qualities;
and just as that world-system Sukhāvatī is, so shall that buddha-field be."
The noble bodhisattvas there will be born spontaneously and will sit cross-legged;
such will that buddha-field be. Then that girl, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and serenity, set out for her own home.
Then the Blessed One said this to that girl:
"Girl, on the seventh day you will die; having died,"
In the eastern direction, in the realm of Magadha, there is a king named Ajitasena.
That King Ajitasena has a harem of one thousand women.
Furthermore, you shall be born as the son of that King Ajitasena.
"This shall indeed be your final dwelling in a womb.
Then the Blessed One departed from the great city of Śrāvastī through the western city gate and proceeded toward the Jetavana monastery.
When the Venerable Ānanda saw the Blessed One approaching from afar, he bowed his head at the Blessed One's feet, circumambulated him three times, and addressed the Blessed One in verse:
When you came as an alms-seeker, golden-hued and honored by excellent marks, bearing a form endowed with the thirty-two marks;
Having liberated all sentient beings here.
You have established all beings in happiness; the power of loving-kindness has been bestowed by you upon the entire world, O supreme leader, O Aṇḍanāyaka. Please accept this alms-food.
And you have liberated the world from fear.
Those bodhisattvas here in Jambudvīpa all show you the path.
In the future time after he has entered parinirvāṇa, one should uphold this sutra praised by the Buddha.
After you have entered final nirvāṇa, in a future time when the teaching is being destroyed,
one will uphold this method, this jewel of a sutra.
Then the Venerable Ānanda, having spoken these verses, circumambulated the Blessed One three times and stood before him.
Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Ānanda:
"Go, Ānanda, strike the gaṇḍī."
Those disciples will partake of the alms-food.
Then the Venerable Ānanda addressed the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, what kind of root of merit will there be for the sound of the gong?"
The Blessed One said:
"Listen, Ānanda, I shall proclaim the root of merit of the sound of the gong.
Whatever beings, Ānanda, shall hear the sound of the gong, their five deeds of immediate retribution will be exhausted."
"They shall become irreversible and will swiftly awaken to unsurpassed, perfect, and complete enlightenment.
Ānanda said,
"Blessed One, what kind of roots of merit have those beings planted?"
The Blessed One said:

"Listen, Ānanda! In the future time, in the final age, when I have passed into parinirvāṇa and the true Dharma is in decline—at the time of the disappearance of the true Dharma—whatever sentient beings, whether in villages, towns, market-towns, districts, kingdoms, or royal capitals, or in forest hermitages, shall hear the sound of the gong being struck and shall utter 'Homage to the Buddha,' their five deeds of immediate retribution will be completely exhausted."
"Such, Ānanda, are the roots of merit of the sound of the gong.
Then the Venerable Ānanda struck the gong with calm and profound tranquility.
Then, by the sound of that gong, all those great disciples assembled.
Just as they were seated on their mats and partaking of the alms-food,
there was a great disciple named Nandimitra who had gathered and sat down right there in the midst of the disciples.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Nandimitra, the great disciple.
"Go, Nandimitra, great disciple, to the eastern direction, to the kingdom of Magadha, and perform the service of a spiritual friend for King Ajitasena.
Then the great disciple Nandimitra said this to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, we will not be able to go to that region of the earth."
"Those beings are difficult to approach;
they will deprive me of my life.
Then the Blessed One [addressed] the Venerable...
He spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"Those beings will not even be able to shake a single hair-tip of yours, let alone deprive you of life.
Then, at the time of dawn, the great śrāvaka Nandimitra, having put on a golden-colored robe, went toward the eastern direction, to the royal capital of King Ajitasena in the kingdom of Magadha.
He followed after him.
Then, upon seeing the great śrāvaka Nandimitra, King Ajitasena became satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and happiness. Thereupon, King Ajitasena dispatched a minister.
"Go and bring this bhikṣu here.
Then that minister approached the place where the great śrāvaka Nandimitra was.
Then that minister said this to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra: "Come, great śrāvaka monk; the king commands you. Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra spoke thus to the minister:
"What business do I have with the king? What will the king do for me? Then the minister approached King Ajitasena and spoke to him thus.
And that monk did not come into your presence. Then King Ajitasena dispatched five hundred ministers, yet that monk still did not come into the presence of King Ajitasena.
Then that king, in his very own physical form, approached where the great śrāvaka Nandimitra was;
having approached him, with palms joined in reverence, he spoke thus:
"Come, O monk, enter my royal capital."
Then King Ajitasena, taking that monk by his right hand, entered his own royal capital.
Then King Ajitasena offered a lion-throne to the monk Nandimitra.
Thereupon, King Ajitasena, having sat down upon a noble seat, spoke thus to that great disciple Nandimitra:
"Where are you going, monk? What is the cause? What is the reason?
Then the great disciple Nandimitra spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"Whosoever have gone forth as monks, they all subsist on almsfood, partaking of it while wandering for alms.
Then King Ajitasena said this to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"Please partake of almsfood at my house."
"I shall provide almsfood for as long as I live.
If you have need of my own flesh, O monk, I will give you my own flesh."
Then the great disciple Nandimitra addressed King Ajitasena in verses:
"I shall eat that food which you give— delicious food and drink, the finest of flavorful drinks."
For you have been liberated from the afflictions; you have obtained the human birth which is so difficult to find.
Extremely difficult to encounter is the teaching of the Leader;
supreme faith and serene confidence are extremely difficult to find,
as are those monks who have gone forth into the teaching.
The teaching of the Leaders is extremely difficult to encounter.
The sight of the most excellent Sugata is very difficult to obtain; homage be to you, O Buddha of great majesty!
Homage be to you, O Great Sage consisting of the Dharma!
Homage be to you, O Noble One who is skilled regarding the afflictions!
Homage be to you, who grant liberation from all aging;
homage be to you, the noble one who reveals the path!
Homage be to you, the shatter of the path; homage be to you, the shatter of the path to awakening.
Then the great disciple Nandimitra, having proclaimed the praise of the Blessed One’s virtues to King Ajitasena, remained silent.
Then the great disciple Nandimitra addressed King Ajitasena with these verses:
"The sight of a monk is likewise very difficult to obtain."
It would be very difficult for them to obtain a vision of him who gives alms to the community of monks.
Neither yakṣas nor rākṣasas have power over him.
Neither pretas, kumbhāṇḍas,
nor mahoragas ever create obstacles for those who give gifts to the community of monks.
Extremely difficult to obtain is his attainment of human birth.
He who maintains the name of the Lord of the World— [a sight] difficult to behold, the state of a monk so exceedingly rare as to be found only after hundreds of inconceivable eons.
For inconceivable billions of nayutas of eons.
He who beholds such a king of monks shall never go to a miserable state of ruin;
for him, there is no falling into a miserable state of ruin.
Whoever beholds such a king of monks.
He who gives almsfood to this one— this alms-collector who has come to me— is my spiritual friend, the one who shows me the path.
Once liberated, they shall no longer suffer from the afflictions of old age and disease.
He shall always be liberated from the afflictions,
and they will give him almsfood here in this world.
Then King Ajitasena, having extolled the praise of the virtues of the great śrāvaka Nandimitra, remained silent.
Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"So be it, Great King; I shall eat almsfood in your house.
Then King Ajitasena satisfied that great disciple Nandimitra with various kinds of solid and soft food.
Thereupon, the great disciple Nandimitra spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"Great King, do you have a pleasure grove in this region of the earth?
The king replied, "Yes, Great Śrāvaka, I have a pleasure grove that is delightful and very beautiful."
Nandimitra said:
"I shall go, O Great King;
I will visit that park."
The king said,
"Go, Nandimitra;
inspect the park grounds."
Then the great disciple Nandimitra approached the park grounds of King Ajitasena.
Now, in those park grounds, all the qualities of a park were present:
the summer lotus ponds were filled with cool water, and the monsoon ponds were filled with water that was neither too warm nor too cold.
And those lotus ponds are covered with golden stairways, divine and delightful;
all those qualities of enjoyment found in Jambūdvīpa are present there,
as are flowers such as the *adhimuktaka*, *campaka*, *aśoka*, *mucilinda*, *pāṭala*, *sumanā*, and *saugandhika*.
(Asv 120) Those birds belonging to the animal realm— parrots, mainas, ruddy geese, peacocks, cuckoos, and so forth— uttered various cries. Then, right there in that garden grove,
birds appeared that were golden-colored, with golden beaks, golden wings, and golden feet.
They all uttered the sound of "Buddha.
Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra approached the royal capital of King Ajitasena. Thereupon, King Ajitasena spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"You have arrived, O great śrāvaka; you have seen the grounds of the pleasure grove.
Nandimitra said:
"I have seen the garden grounds, delightful and most beautiful.
Then King Ajitasena addressed the great śrāvaka Nandimitra with these verses:
"Those things which were for enjoyment in Jambudvīpa..."
The *adhimuktaka*, *campaka*, and *dhānuṣkārika*; likewise the *aśoka*, *mucilinda*, *pāṭalā*,
*saugandhika*, *sumanā*, and *vārṣikā*.
Then the Pāriyātra mountain, situated on the riverbank,
became golden in color and was always filled with birds; and they showed the way to supreme enlightenment.
And they shall constantly cause divine, pleasing, and sweet sounds to be heard.
Then the great disciple Nandimitra, having spoken these verses to King Ajitasena, remained silent.
Thereupon, King Ajitasena struck the drum.
Then, gathered by the sound of that drum, the assembly of ministers spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"For whose sake, Great King, has the drum been beaten?
Then the king said, "Let the elephant-chariots and horse-chariots be made ready."
"I shall go to the park grounds for the sake of sport.
Then, having heard those words, those millions of ministers quickly prepared that elephant-chariot and horse-chariot.
Then, in a mere instant, a brief moment, and a short duration, King Ajitasena arrived at the place where the park grounds were located.
And that great śrāvaka Nandimitra approached the king Ajitasena and said to him:
"Great King, a small hut should be built for me on this spot of ground, where I may sit and partake of alms-food in your palace.
Then King Ajitasena spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"What kind of hut should be built for you?
Nandimitra said,
"O Great King, it should be just like yours."
"With such great resolve, faith, and serene confidence, have such a hut constructed.
Then King Ajitasena said to his chief minister:
"Have a hut constructed on this very spot of earth."
Then the senior minister spoke thus to the king:
"O Great King, what kind of hut should I have built?
King Ajitasena replied as follows:
"Have a small hut constructed, thirty yojanas in length and six yojanas in height, made of the seven precious gems and covered with jewels and pearls. Then that minister had the hut constructed,
made of the seven precious gems.
Having had it covered with jewels and pearls, he approached King Ajitasena and said to him:
"Great King, I have constructed the hut exactly as you commanded.
The king said:
On that very spot of earth, a walking path (*caṅkrama*) should be constructed, four *yojanas* in length and two *yojanas* in width.
Then, having had that walking path constructed, the minister approached King Ajitasena and addressed the king with verses:
"I have well and beautifully constructed the walking path."
O Lord, that which was previously accomplished by you is indeed this:
that you liberate beings from their nature; you shall liberate all these living creatures from both the auspicious and the inauspicious.
Oh, how well-gained is what you have vowed!
You shall liberate the entire world together with its gods;
for such a vow as this has been made by you.
I am a Dharma-preacher who illuminates the Dharma.
Having sat down, you have established a small hut and a walking path;
whatever has been done by you has been done in such a way that even the walking path you have made is most beautiful.
That ground was completely covered with precious jewels.
Then King Ajitasena departed for his own royal capital.
Thereupon, the great śrāvaka Nandimitra, having returned, sat down right there in that very hut and entered the bodhisattva-samādhi called Vikiraṇa.

With one [hand] he reached for his hair, with another his eyes, with another his teeth, with another his neck, with another his arms, with another his heart, with another his belly, with another his thighs, with another his shanks, and with another his feet; thus he was completely overcome. Then, after the passing of seven days, King Ajitasena did not see that monk.
Then the king said to his eldest son:
"Come, noble son; I shall go to that hut.
I will approach the place where that monk is."
Then that king, together with his son, approached the place where that hut was located.
When King Ajitasena saw that the monk’s body had been cut into pieces, he was seized by doubt;
his hair stood on end with terror, and tearing at his clothes, lamenting and weeping with a throat choked by tears, he spoke thus to his son:
"Bring me, my son, a sharp-edged sword;
I shall deprive myself of life.
Then the prince, with palms joined in reverence, addressed the king in verses:
O King of Men, do not let your mind be filled with grief,
nor experience such sensations;
for by committing suicide, you will go to hell.
And you shall also go to the most dreadful hell, Raurava.
...This one is worthy of offerings in the world, the liberator from old age and disease;
yet he was not slain by yakṣas, nor by bhūtas, nor by rākṣasas.
This Bodhisattva too is in the world the liberator from old age and disease.
He is worthy of offerings in this world, the liberator from old age and disease;
rare is the sight of him, the one who reveals the path to awakening.
This spiritual friend has come for your sake;
he is worthy of offerings in this world, and I am the one who brings happiness to all sentient beings.
To the omniscient one who has attained the perfections, sent by the Lord of the World—
the Great Seer, the Lord of the World, possessed of firm vigor and steadfast power.
Whoever holds its name in mind does not go to an evil state;
they shall not go to a place of misery, but will be reborn in the heavenly world.
Then that prince, having spoken this verse to his father, remained silent.
Thereupon King Ajitasena said to his own son:
"How do you know, prince, that this monk had entered into meditative absorption?"
Then that prince spoke thus:

"Behold, Great King, this monk has entered the samādhi of a bodhisattva; he is completely liberated from all afflictions, has reached the further shore of the ocean of existence, and for the sake of the welfare of all sentient beings, he demonstrates the auspicious path."
Then that prince said this to the king:
"Come, father, we shall go to the walking-paths.
Then the king and the prince, together with many hundreds of boys, approached the place where those walking-paths were located.
Then that monk, having emerged from that samādhi, spoke thus to King Ajitasena:
"Come, Great King; what are you doing in this place?
Then the king, seeing the monk, gave his crown-ribbon to the prince.
"Let your kingdom be yours;
protect it through righteousness, not through unrighteousness.
The prince said:
I have performed many countless royal duties,
yet never was there satisfaction.
O father, let the kingdom be yours.
"I have no need for the kingdom, nor for enjoyments, nor for sovereignty and lordship.
Let the kingdom be yours, father;
I shall protect it through righteousness, not through unrighteousness."
Then the king approached that monk and, with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus:
"O Sage, it is very difficult to obtain a vision of you, the Leaders; I stand before you with my hands joined in salutation."
The seers have shown you the arrival of liberation,
which is extremely difficult to attain even through hundreds of inconceivable karmas.
Those ṛṣis who shall grant you their vision will be liberated for ten million eons;
they shall never go to the miserable states of ruin or evil rebirths.
Whoever hears the name for even a moment.
The king said:
"Seated upon a beautiful, jewel-encrusted vehicle, I shall go to where that royal capital lies."
I give abundant food;
I give these garments of Kāśī cloth.
And these fine, closely woven nets of cloth which I give to you as a robe today.
Then that monk, taking a palanquin made of jewels, approached the royal capital.
Having been fully satisfied with food,
the great disciple Nandimitra then addressed King Ajitasena in verses:
Those who give to the community of monks a gift of abundant food— excellent, pure, and delicious with the flavors of fine meals and drinks— satisfy them completely.
They will go to the seat of awakening after a long time.
The sight of the Leader is very difficult to obtain; before long, he will go to the excellent buddha-field of Amitāyus.
One goes quickly to Sukhāvatī; this is so.
Then the great śrāvaka Nandimitra, having spoken these verses to King Ajitasena, remained silent.
Then King Ajitasena struck the drum.
Then, by the sound of that drum, all those tens of millions of ministers said this to the king:
"For whose sake, Great King, has the drum been beaten?
The king replied,
"On the seventh day, the elephant-chariots and horse-chariots must be made ready."
"On the seventh day, I shall go to the monastery named Jetavana to see, pay homage to, attend upon, and listen to the Dharma from the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha.
Then the ten million ministers said this to King Ajitasena:
"Great King, we have prepared the elephant-chariots and horse-chariots.
Then King Ajitasena, having descended from his elephant-chariot and having helped the great śrāvaka Nandimitra descend from his jewel-encrusted chariot, proceeded toward the Jetavana monastery.
When the Blessed One saw King Ajitasena approaching from afar, he addressed all the śrāvakas.
"All must display various miraculous transformations.
Then, all those great śrāvakas entered the bodhisattva-samādhi named Jvālāmāla.
Then the king, seeing from afar that mountain garlanded with flames, spoke thus to the great śrāvaka Nandimitra:
"For whose sake do I see this mountain become garlanded with flames?
Nandimitra replied:
There, the Tathāgata Śākyamuni, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, remains, stays, and maintains himself, and he teaches the Dharma.
Those bodhisattvas have entered the bodhisattva-samādhi called Jvālāmāla.
Then King Ajitasena, having descended from his elephant-chariot, approached the Blessed One on foot together with his thousand sons.
Then the Blessed One walked with a body of golden hue and a fathom-wide radiance.
Then King Ajitasena, having seen the Blessed One’s form, color, marks, and shape, fainted and fell to the ground.
Thereupon the Blessed One extended his golden-colored arm and raised the king up.
"Arise, Great King! For whose sake have you fallen down? The king said:
"Throughout many inconceivable eons, and hundreds of millions of inconceivable births..."
Never before have I seen your form here, you who are the Lord of the World and the most worthy recipient of offerings.
O Sage, caravan leader, you who deliver from old age and disease, golden-hued, with limbs endowed with excellent marks,
and bearing the thirty-two characteristics!
He who beholds the form of the Lord of the World never goes to a state of woe;
therefore, O Lord of the World, I bow my head in homage to you.
Then King Ajitasena, with palms joined in reverence, spoke thus to the Blessed One:
"Blessed One, I shall go forth into homelessness in your teaching.
Thereupon, the Blessed One was pleased, uplifted, joyful, delighted, and filled with a sense of gladness and serenity.
To those who had not yet attained their goal, he said this to King Ajitasena, whose teaching was widespread there:
"Go, Great King, to your own home; on the seventh day, I shall come."

Then King Ajitasena, satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and cheerfulness, having placed that virtuous friend, the monk, before him, went to his own palace and addressed all his ministers:
"The roads must be cleared by all the villages, towns, market-towns, and provinces; banners made of jewels must be raised in every house."
"The jars must be filled.
Then all those ministers gave the command;
the roads were cleared by all the villages, cities, towns, and districts, banners were raised, and jars made of jewels were filled.
Where King Ajitasena dwelt, there twelve koṭis of victory banners were raised and twelve koṭis of jeweled jars were filled.

Then, on the seventh day, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, surrounded and escorted by a great saṅgha of śrāvakas headed by Śāriputra, Maudgalyāyana, Ānanda, and Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra, arrived at the royal capital of King Ajitasena.
Then King Ajitasena, taking a basket of flowers and placing his spiritual friend before him, scattered flowers over the Blessed One and addressed the Blessed One in this way:
"By this root of merit, may all sentient beings realize unexcelled, perfect, and complete enlightenment."
Then King Ajitasena prepared seats;
he offered a lion-throne to that Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One sat upon the lion-throne and taught the Dharma to King Ajitasena.
Then King Ajitasena satisfied him with abundant food, both solid and soft;
then King Ajitasena gave his eldest son, the prince, saying,
"Ordain this prince."
"Therefore, I shall go forth later.
Then the Blessed One addressed the venerable Ānanda:
"Go, Ānanda, and ordain this prince."
(Asv 130) Then the venerable Ānanda ordained that prince;
as soon as he had been ordained, he attained the fruit of arhatship and beheld all the buddha-fields.
Then the prince, positioned in the air, addressed his father with these verses:
"Do not delay, dear father; do not undergo any distress."
Oh, what a great gain is the sight of the Sugatas!
Oh, what a great gain is the attainment of the Sugatas!
Oh, how well-gained is this supreme gain, the attainment of renunciation praised by the Sugata!
Liberation from saṃsāra has been praised by the Sugata.
Go forth into homelessness quickly, my dear; do not delay!
Do not cause distress to the Lord of the Leaders of the World; having obtained this human birth which is so very difficult to find, the sight of the Leaders is likewise exceedingly rare.
Having gone forth quickly, I have indeed attained and realized the supreme, foremost awakening;
yet, having heard those words of his son, the king did not then [act].
He went forth into homelessness in the teaching of the Guide.
Then the prince, having ascended into the air, spoke this verse and remained silent.

Thereupon, King Ajitasena, having heard his son’s words, was satisfied, elated, joyful, delighted, and filled with gladness and serenity; he caused a monastery to be built dedicated to the Blessed One.
Ten million musical instruments were presented to her;
within her thousandfold harem, the female organs disappeared and male organs appeared.
Then King Ajitasena went forth into homelessness in the teaching of the Blessed One.
Those tens of millions of ministers went forth in the teaching of the Blessed One,
and those thousands of men from the inner court also went forth.
Having caused King Ajitasena to go forth, the Blessed One set out for the Jetavana monastery.
Then the venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:
"This King Ajitasena, having renounced his kingdom and caused a monastery to be built, has gone forth in the teaching of the Blessed One.
What kind of root of merit will he possess?"
The Blessed One said: "Excellent, excellent, Ānanda, that which you have proclaimed!
This King Ajitasena shall go forth in my teaching."

In a future time, after immeasurable, inconceivable, and infinite eons, there will appear in the world a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha named Ajitaprabha— one perfected in knowledge and conduct, a Sugata, a knower of the world, an unsurpassed charioteer of men to be tamed, a teacher of gods and humans, a Buddha, a Blessed One.
Ānanda said:
"This great śrāvaka Nandimitra was the king’s spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra).
What kind of root of merit (kuśalamūla) will he possess?"
The Blessed One said:
"Ānanda, at that very time, this great śrāvaka Nandimitra will appear in the world as a Tathāgata, Arhat, and Samyaksaṃbuddha named Nandiprabha.
Ānanda said:

"Blessed One, what will the buddha-field of those Tathāgatas be like? The Blessed One said, "That buddha-field where these Tathāgatas will appear shall be named *Aparimitaguṇasaṃcaya* (Accumulation of Immeasurable Qualities). Ānanda said:
"What kind of mass of merit will belong to one who, in the final age, in the final time, shall fully proclaim this entire dharma-discourse?
The Blessed One said:
"Ānanda, when I have awakened to enlightenment after practicing hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of difficult deeds, then those beings shall awaken to enlightenment."
"Those who hear even a single four-line verse from this Dharma-discourse will become beings irreversible from unexcelled, perfect enlightenment.
Ānanda said,
"What kind of roots of merit will those Dharma-preachers possess who shall fully proclaim this Dharma-discourse?"

The Blessed One said: "Listen, Ānanda! He who shall fully proclaim this entire discourse on the Dharma in its completion will become a universal monarch (cakravartin), the lord of the four continents; and he shall be liberated, freed from birth, old age, sickness, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair."
"They will come to be. Ānanda said:
"In the future time, in the final age, what will be the destiny of those beings who reject this Dharma-discourse and do not believe it? What will be their refuge?
The Blessed One said:
Enough, enough, Ānanda!
Do not ask me about that mass of evil karma;
it is impossible for me to describe it in full.
"Except by millions of Buddhas, it cannot be fully proclaimed.
Ānanda said, "Proclaim it, Blessed One! Proclaim it!"
The Sugata, the Blessed One, said:
"Listen, Ānanda, I shall proclaim the destiny of one who rejects the true Dharma.

He must experience suffering for many thousands of eons in the great Raurava hell, the great Hahava hell, the great Huhuva hell, the Avīci great hell, in the animal realm, in the world of Yama, and in the domain of the hungry ghosts."
If they should ever be reborn in the world of humans, their throat and palate will be long and parched;
their tongue will be twelve yojanas in length,
and twelve plows will pass over it for those who speak such words.
"O noble sons, do not ever reject the true Dharma!
Such is the destiny of one who rejects the true Dharma. Ānanda said:
"For what reason, Blessed One, is the true Dharma rejected?
The Blessed One said:

Those beings who, in the final age, in the final time, will revile, scold, despise, and disparage these Dharma-preachers who uphold these sūtras, and who will give rise to malicious thoughts toward those Dharma-preachers—
for them, the True Dharma will have been rejected.
If a person were to pluck out the eyes of all sentient beings in the triple-thousand great-thousandfold world system, the mass of demerit resulting from that would be far greater than this;
likewise, whoever looks upon these upholders of the sūtras and preachers of the Dharma with a malicious mind will produce an even greater mass of demerit than that.
Then Ānanda replied with verses to the Blessed One:
"I have heard many thousands of sūtras from the presence of the Teacher,
yet never before have I heard a sūtra such as this."
After the Teacher has passed into parinirvāṇa, in a most terrifying future time,
I shall proclaim this sūtra and uphold this method.
In this jewel of a sūtra which will exist in the future time,
I shall provide protection for them during that most terrifying later age.
I shall reject this profound teaching spoken by the Buddha.
Then the Venerable Ānanda, having spoken a verse to the Blessed One, stood silent.
Then the Great Disciple Kāśyapa addressed the Blessed One with verses:
"O you whose limbs possess the excellent marks and a golden hue..."
To the Jina who bears the thirty-two marks,
[I offer] this well-spoken sutra of great power,
profound in dharma, subtle, and very difficult to perceive.
This unsurpassed sūtra has been revealed;
may it not be lost in the future time after the Jina has entered parinirvāṇa.
"I shall uphold this unsurpassed method of the sūtra.
Then the Venerable Śāradvatīputra addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"Homage be to you, O Buddha of great majesty!"
This unsurpassed sūtra has been revealed;
O Leader of the World, after you have entered final nirvāṇa, they shall write down this unsurpassed sūtra.
Nor does he go to the fear of miserable rebirths;
rather, he goes swiftly to heaven.
Then the venerable Pūrṇa Maitrāyaṇīputra addressed the Blessed One in verses:
“Grateful to many beings, you are their deliverer from the fear of miserable rebirths.
You have revealed this profound sūtra, which is the right-hand path of the Buddhas.”
"For in the final age, after you, the Leader, have entered parinirvāṇa,
I shall proclaim this sūtra for the benefit of all living beings.
Thus spoke Brahmā Sahāmpati to the Blessed One in verses.
Homage be to you, O Buddha of great power;
this auspicious sūtra has been revealed by you.
O Leader of the World, once you have entered final nirvana, I shall indeed provide protection for this jewel of a sutra.
Then the four great kings addressed the Blessed One in verses:
"Aha! This most beautiful and excellent jewel of a sūtra has been revealed at such a time as this, in the final age."
...he beholds this jewel of a sutra revealed in the final age.
I shall indeed uphold this jewel of a sutra of the Sugatas, the guides of the world;
I shall provide protection for this jewel of a sutra.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, his mind filled with joy.
And that entire assembly rejoiced in what the Blessed One had spoken.
The Mahāyāna sūtra titled "The Exposition of the Prophecy of Ajitasena" is completed.
This is the religious gift of Bālosiṃha, together with his wife Jājatitrana; together with his parents, who were his greatest benefactors;
together with Kṣiṇīena, Akhiloṭia, Diśoṭāja, Maṅgali..., Utrayannagarvidoṭia, Vaṭrari-khuśoṭi, and Khuśogoṭia;
and together with all sentient beings and all [beings]... whatever merit there is in this, may it be for the unsurpassed [enlightenment] of all sentient beings.
... together with his steadfast kinsman, the supreme spiritual friend;
this book was written by the Dharma-preacher Narendra-datta.
